question: A person lost 15% by selling an item for ₹5,270. If he had sold the item for ₹6,324, then what would his profit or loss percentage have been?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Loss is 15% when SP is Rs. 5,270

⇒ 5270 = 85% of CP

⇒ 6324 = 85/5270 × 6324 = 102% of CP

⇒ Second SP(6324) is 102% of CP

∴ There will be a profit of 2%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

First SP = Rs. 5,270

Loss incurred = 15%

Second SP = Rs. 6,324

**Formula used:**

CP = SP × 100/(100 - Loss%)

Profit = SP - CP

Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

According to the questions,

Loss is 15% when SP is Rs

So, CP = 5270 × 100/(100 - 15) = Rs. 6200

When the article is sold at Rs. 6,324

Profit = 6324 - 6200 = 124

Profit% = (124/6200) × 100 = 2%

**∴ The profit percentage is 2%**
